factual_errors.claim: Citation [1] to a related CompactLogix/ControlLogix manual page supports the DH-485 protocol-mismatch claim
factual_errors.why_wrong: The cited source documents (1769-um011, 1756-rm003) are CompactLogix/ControlLogix literature, an EtherNet/IP-era platform family, not the legacy SLC 5/03 DH-485 network. The answer is honest that this is 'the closest match' and may differ, but the specific claim about DH-485 half-duplex wiring/termination is unlikely to actually be substantiated by that source -- this is weak, likely-mismatched grounding presented with a citation marker.

factual_errors.claim: No mention of the 0-5V RS-485 vs Ethernet voltage damage risk
factual_errors.why_wrong: Same critical equipment-damage omission as the ungrounded version of this answer: connecting standard Ethernet-voltage equipment to the DH-485 RJ45 port can damage the network card or processor. Still missing here.

notes: Better-behaved than the ungrounded version: it discloses the source is a related-but-not-exact manual and tells the user to confirm before acting, and adds an explicit LOTO reminder. But the cited pages are from a different controller family and likely don't substantiate the specific DH-485 claim, so evidence is weak despite the citation marker. Still omits TX-EN/token-passing detail, the definitive fix (protocol-aware interface), and the voltage-damage warning.
